title: HubSpot’s Co-Founder on Finding Your Next Startup Idea
content: HubSpot co-founder Dharmesh Shah and a16z partner Joe Schmidt discuss startup strategies amidst AI expansion. They recommend avoiding direct competition with AI labs by focusing on narrow markets and solving whole customer problems. As models become infrastructure, application companies can build lasting value through workflows and customer context. Shah also highlights how cheaper software creation unlocks previously unsupportive markets and notes the rise of one-person businesses, drawing on HubSpot’s evolution to guide founders toward sustainable opportunities.

title: [开源]OxideTerm： Rust+GPUI，让终端飞起来！
content: OxideTerm is an open-source, cross-platform terminal and SSH client written in Rust using the GPUI framework. It supports protocols such as SSH, SFTP, Mosh, RDP, and VNC. Recent updates focus on performance, significantly improving throughput and reducing memory consumption for large logs. Features include native plugins, local semantic coloring, a draggable SFTP sidebar, X11 forwarding, and an MCP interface for AI integration. Licensed under GPL-3.0, OxideTerm is free, requires no account, and does not collect telemetry data, targeting users seeking a lightweight alternative to established terminals like WindTerm.

title: 感觉 AI Agent Coding 时代开源与 AI 的对话 sessions 比开源源代码更有意义（因为代码已经没人看了，开发者与 AI 的交互反而更重要）
content: In the AI Agent Coding era, developer-AI conversation sessions are becoming more valuable than source code. While sessions act as critical "meta-assets," they contain sensitive data such as API keys, local paths, and proprietary information. Therefore, publicly releasing them requires rigorous sanitization. Future standards should distinguish between raw and anonymized sessions, linking them to Git commits, preserving prompt and tool interactions, and enabling partial replay. However, replaying a session does not guarantee reproducible development, as results depend on model versions, context, and execution environments.

Operating under the brand Xiaolu Aixue, the company focuses on leveraging AI to support students’ long-term growth and overcome technological limitations. content: Anthropic launched Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, models claiming superior performance over predecessors in coding, science, and cyber capabilities. Highlights include a 30-hour formal proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem by 1,000 agents, autonomous operating system creation, and hardware design. Fable 5.2 is the public version with safety constraints, while Mythos 5.2 offers unrestricted capabilities for specialized sectors. Both models feature improved speed, reduced pricing, and enhanced anti-distillation protections. Anthropic reports that Fable 5.2 was deliberately limited in specific AI research areas to prevent recursive self-improvement.
